title: Fusion-3D: Integrated Acceleration for Instant 3D Reconstruction and Real-Time Rendering
problem: Current NeRF acceleration techniques lack end-to-end pipeline acceleration support, causing impractical off-chip bandwidth demands for edge devices in AR/VR applications. Additionally, existing approaches have limited scalability for handling large-scale 3D scenes.
motivation: Recent NeRF breakthroughs enable immersive AR/VR experiences but require practical acceleration to meet real-time and bandwidth constraints of edge devices.
method: Fusion-3D implements a specialized end-to-end processor for all three NeRF pipeline stages, featuring dynamic scheduling and hardware-aware sampling in the reconstruction stage, plus a shared reconfigurable pipeline with mixed-precision arithmetic for training and rendering. For large scenes, a multi-chip architecture employs a three-level hierarchical tiling scheme that minimizes inter-chip communication and balances workloads across multiple 28nm CMOS chips.
key_novelty: First end-to-end NeRF pipeline accelerator achieving both instant 3D reconstruction (≤2 seconds) and real-time rendering (≥30 FPS) while requiring only USB-port-level bandwidth (0.625 GB/s).
contributions: End-to-end processor design with dynamic scheduling and hardware-aware sampling for NeRF pipeline stages
Shared reconfigurable pipeline with mixed-precision arithmetic for efficient training and inference
Multi-chip architecture with hierarchical tiling scheme for scalable large-scene handling
Prototype tape-out in 28nm CMOS demonstrating 2.5-6x speedup over SOTA accelerators and 7.3-6.5x over Nvidia 2080Ti

metrics.speedup: 2.5x (training) and 6x (inference) vs SOTA; 7.3x (training) and 6.5x (inference) vs Nvidia 2080Ti

primary_theme: end-to-end NeRF acceleration for edge devices
